description: The second record of a deployment's start stream, and the first thing the customer attests. Signed by the bootstrap key and then by one of the customer's root keys. It accepts the start record before it and names the customer's roots, how many must act together, and any recovery keys. Its reference is the chain's name. After it the bootstrap key has no authority.

accepts.description: The ChainStarted record at position 1 of this stream.

claimedBy.description: The root key that signs this record for the customer. It must be one of the roots listed.

custodians.description: The people who may approve a change of roots. A person is named first; their own key may be given here or bound to them later.

identity.description: A stable identity written as a URI. Syntax is not authentication.

details.description: Issuer-defined detail: up to 64 named scalars. Nothing in it is interpreted by the base kinds, and nothing in it is content; content goes behind a reference.

recoveryKeys.description: Key ids of recovery keys. A key id is a fingerprint of the public key, so the key itself stays unrevealed until it is used.

identity.description: A stable identity written as a URI. Syntax is not authentication.

publicKey.description: A public key: a registered algorithm and the key's bytes in strict padded base64.

threshold.description: How many of the roots must act together to change these terms.
